newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends lower on late dollar-buying.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends lower on late dollar-buying.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed weaker at 26.378 to the dollar on Wednesday following late dollar-buying by some banks, traders said.
"Some foreign banks started buying dollars in late afternoon, speculating that the Central Bank may raise its dollar selling rate again on Friday ... But I doubt it will do that," one trader said.
The peso closed at 26.373 on Tuesday.
Last Friday, the Central Bank increased its dollar selling rate to 26.390 saying it was a preemptive move to prevent market players from taking advantage of the weekend swap points.

The move created a mild panic in the market since banks thought the Central Bank was willing to let the peso depreciate. The Central Bank later retracted its move and adjusted its rate back to the market rate.

Another trader attributed the dollar-buying to the swap points earned on a one-day holiday on Thursday. The foreign exchange market will be closed on Thursday for independence day. Trading will resume Friday.
A total of $178 million changed hands with rates fluctuating from 26.367 to 26.378.
